target_constraint: Must withstand 10+ million gait cycles without fracture
observed_phenomenon: Tibial tray fracture under cyclic loading
mechanism: The evidence indicates that mechanical failure at implant interfaces can occur due to dissociation or breakage under load, and that structural failure mechanisms are a recognized concern in implant design, particularly at modular junctions or load-bearing components.
intervention: Redesign the tibial tray to eliminate or reinforce the modular junction between the tray and its stem or locking mechanism, using a monolithic (single-piece) construction or adding a load-distributing lateral support plate at the tray's high-stress region to prevent fracture propagation under cyclic gait loading.
expected_effect: By removing the modular interface or reinforcing the load-bearing area, stress concentrations that initiate fatigue cracks are reduced, allowing the tray to withstand 10+ million gait cycles without fracture.
falsification_test: Subject the redesigned tibial tray to ISO 14879-1 cyclic loading (10 million cycles at 3× body weight) and compare crack initiation and fracture rates against the baseline cobalt-chromium tray; failure is defined as any visible crack or fracture before 10 million cycles.
